source_title: Guideline Based Management of Abdominal Discomfort in Elderly: A Clinical Flow Chart Guide
text:
Condition: GORD (Gastro-oesophageal Reflux Disease)
Key features: Heartburn, regurgitation; Worse at night or after meals; Atypical symptoms: cough, hoarseness, asthma; Consider drug-induced (nitrates, CCBs); Alarm symptoms: weight loss, dysphagia
Investigations: Clinical diagnosis; Upper GI endoscopy if alarm symptoms or long-standing; pH monitoring (if refractory)
Initial/conservative management: Lifestyle: weight reduction, elevate head end, avoid late meals, reduce trigger foods; Trial PPI once daily (e.g., Pantoprazole 40 mg OD); Antacids / alginates PRN
Advanced/specific management: Optimize PPI (BD dosing if needed); Add H2 blocker at night if nocturnal symptoms; Evaluate & stop offending drugs; Endoscopic evaluation if alarm or refractory; Consider surgery (fundoplication) in fit patients with refractory disease
Follow-up: Review in 4-8 weeks; Monitor symptom control; Watch for B12 deficiency, fractures (long-term PPI); Repeat endoscopy if symptoms persist or worsen

red_flags: Severe abdominal pain with guarding or rigidity

source_title: Guideline Based Management of Abdominal Discomfort in Elderly: A Clinical Flow Chart Guide
text:
Condition: Peptic Ulcer Disease (PUD)
Key features: Epigastric pain, burning; Pain related to meals (DU: pain after, GU: pain with food); NSAID use common in elderly; Alarm: bleeding, anemia, weight loss, vomiting
Investigations: Upper GI endoscopy (gold standard); H. pylori test (Urea breath test / stool antigen / biopsy)
Initial/conservative management: Stop NSAIDs; Start PPI (e.g., Pantoprazole 40 mg BD); Test & treat H. pylori if positive; Sucralfate if needed
Advanced/specific management: H. pylori eradication: PPI + Clarithromycin + Amoxicillin (or Metronidazole) for 14 days; Continue PPI 4-8 weeks (DU), 8-12 weeks (GU); Endoscopic therapy if bleeding; Surgery if perforation, obstruction, recurrent bleeding
Follow-up: Confirm H. pylori eradication; Monitor for anemia; Avoid NSAIDs (use alternatives); Repeat endoscopy if non-healing ulcer or alarm

text:
Condition: Gall Bladder Diseases
Key features: RUQ pain, nausea, bloating; Pain after fatty meals; May have fever (cholecystitis); Elderly may present atypically; Consider comorbid cardiac/pulmonary disease
Investigations: Ultrasound abdomen (first line); LFT, CBC; Consider HIDA scan if biliary dyskinesia suspected
Initial/conservative management: Analgesia (Paracetamol); Low-fat diet; Hydration; Treat infection if present (Antibiotics)
Advanced/specific management: Cholelithiasis (symptomatic): Laparoscopic cholecystectomy (preferred) if fit; Acute cholecystitis: IV antibiotics + supportive care; Percutaneous cholecystostomy if high surgical risk; ERCP if choledocholithiasis
Follow-up: Monitor LFT, symptoms; Post-op follow-up; Watch for complications (jaundice, pancreatitis); Dietary advice
red_flags: Severe abdominal pain with guarding or rigidity

source_title: Guideline Based Management of Abdominal Discomfort in Elderly: A Clinical Flow Chart Guide
text:
Condition: Gastric Carcinoma
Key features: Early satiety, bloating; Weight loss, anorexia; Epigastric discomfort; Anemia, occult bleeding; More common in >70 yrs; Alarm symptoms common
Investigations: Upper GI endoscopy with biopsy; CT abdomen (staging); CBC, LFT, tumor markers (CEA, CA19-9)
Initial/conservative management: Nutritional support; Treat anemia; Pain control; PPI for symptom relief
Advanced/specific management: Multidisciplinary approach; Surgery (if early & resectable); Chemotherapy (e.g., FLOT regimen); Radiotherapy (adjuvant / palliative); Palliative care for advanced disease; Endoscopic stenting for obstruction
Follow-up: Regular oncology follow-up; Monitor nutrition & weight; Manage complications; Psychosocial support
red_flags: Severe abdominal pain with guarding or rigidity

source_title: Guideline Based Management of Abdominal Discomfort in Elderly: A Clinical Flow Chart Guide

Condition: Bowel Cancer (Colorectal Cancer)
Key features: Change in bowel habits; Rectal bleeding; Abdominal discomfort; Iron deficiency anemia; Weight loss, fatigue; High prevalence in elderly
Investigations: Colonoscopy with biopsy; CEA level; CT abdomen/pelvis (staging)
Initial/conservative management: Nutritional assessment; Treat anemia; Pain relief; Bowel regimen
Advanced/specific management: Surgery (curative if early stage); Chemotherapy (adjuvant / palliative); Radiotherapy (rectal cancer); Targeted therapy (selected cases); Palliative stoma for obstruction
Follow-up: Surveillance colonoscopy (as per guidelines); Monitor CEA; Manage side effects of treatment; Supportive care

source_title: Guideline Based Management of Abdominal Discomfort in Elderly: A Clinical Flow Chart Guide
text:
Condition: Diverticulitis
Key features: LLQ pain; Fever, altered bowel habits; Nausea, bloating; May present with confusion in elderly; Consider perforation risk
Investigations: Clinical diagnosis; CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast (gold standard); CBC, CRP
Initial/conservative management: Mild (uncomplicated): Oral antibiotics (e.g., Amoxicillin-Clavulanate or Ciprofloxacin + Metronidazole); Low residue diet; Hydration; Analgesia
Advanced/specific management: Severe / complicated: IV antibiotics; Abscess: percutaneous drainage; Peritonitis, fistula, obstruction: Surgical management; Elective surgery for recurrent episodes
Follow-up: Monitor symptoms; Colonoscopy after recovery (6-8 weeks); High fibre diet after recovery; Prevent constipation

red_flags: Severe abdominal pain with guarding or rigidity

management_conservative: Mild (uncomplicated): Oral antibiotics (e.g., Amoxicillin-Clavulanate or Ciprofloxacin + Metronidazole)

source_title: Guideline Based Management of Abdominal Discomfort in Elderly: A Clinical Flow Chart Guide
text:
Condition: Bowel Obstruction
Key features: Colicky abdominal pain; Vomiting; Abdominal distension; Constipation / obstipation; High risk in elderly (adhesions, hernia, tumors)
Investigations: Clinical diagnosis; X-ray abdomen (erect); CT abdomen (if unclear); Labs (U&E, CBC)
Initial/conservative management: NPO (nil by mouth); IV fluids & electrolytes; Nasogastric decompression; Analgesia; Treat underlying cause if infection
Advanced/specific management: Conservative management: adhesive obstruction (no strangulation); Surgery for bowel strangulation, ischemia, perforation, or failure of conservative therapy; Endoscopic stenting (selected cases)
Follow-up: Monitor vitals, abdominal signs; Repeat imaging if no improvement; Nutritional support; Prevent recurrence

management_advanced: Surgery for bowel strangulation, ischemia, perforation, or failure of conservative therapy

text:
Condition: Migraines
Key features: Unilateral, throbbing; Moderate to severe; Nausea / vomiting; Photophobia / phonophobia; Aura (visual, sensory) may precede; Worse with activity
Investigations: Usually clinical; Neuroimaging if atypical features or red flags
Initial/conservative management: Trigger avoidance; Regular sleep & meals; Hydration; Stress management; Relaxation therapy; Biofeedback
Advanced/specific management: Ibuprofen 400-800 mg PO stat, then 400-800 mg q6-8h PRN (max 2400 mg/day) - up to 3-5 days; Sumatriptan 50-100 mg PO at onset; may repeat 50-100 mg after 2 h (max 200 mg/24 h) - up to 2 days/week; Metoclopramide 10 mg PO/IV q8h PRN for nausea - up to 3 days; Topiramate 25 mg HS titrate to 50-100 mg/day - >= 3 months; Propranolol 20 mg BID titrate to 40-80 mg BID - >= 3 months; Amitriptyline 10-25 mg HS titrate to 25-75 mg HS - >= 3 months
Differential red flags: Sudden severe onset; Neurological deficit; New onset > 50 yrs; Change in pattern; Fever / stiff neck

source_title: Evaluation of Headache in Adults: A Clinical Flow Chart Guide
text:
Condition: Cluster Headache
Key features: Severe, unilateral (around eye); Sharp / piercing; Lasts 15-180 min; Red eye, tearing, nasal congestion; Restlessness / agitation; Occurs in clusters
Investigations: Usually clinical; Imaging to rule out secondary causes if atypical
Initial/conservative management: Avoid alcohol during cluster period; Regular sleep; Stress reduction; Identify & avoid triggers
Advanced/specific management: Sumatriptan 6 mg SC stat; may repeat after 1 h (max 12 mg/24 h) - up to 2 attacks/day; Zolmitriptan 5 mg nasal spray stat; may repeat after 2 h (max 10 mg/24 h); Oxygen 100% via non-rebreather mask 12-15 L/min for 15-20 min - each attack; Verapamil 80 mg TID titrate to 240-960 mg/day - >= 6-8 weeks; Prednisone 60 mg daily taper over 2-3 weeks (short term bridge)
Differential red flags: New onset > 40 yrs; Neurological deficit; Change in pattern; Persistent outside cluster periods

Key features: Bilateral, pressing / tightening; Mild to moderate; Not aggravated by routine activity; No nausea / vomiting; Stress / fatigue related

Condition: Brain Tumour
Key features: Progressive headache; Worse in morning; Vomiting; Seizures; Focal neurological deficit; Personality / cognitive changes

text:
Condition: Acute Angle Closure Glaucoma
Key features: Severe eye pain; Headache (often unilateral); Blurred vision / halos around lights; Nausea / vomiting; Red eye
Investigations: Intraocular pressure measurement; Slit lamp exam; Ophthalmology consult
Initial/conservative management: Avoid dark rooms; Immediate ophthalmology referral; Patient education
Differential red flags: Sudden onset; Visual disturbance; Halos around lights; Nausea / vomiting

source_title: Evaluation of Headache in Adults: A Clinical Flow Chart Guide
text:
Condition: Drug Induced Headache
Key features: Temporal relation to drug initiation or dose change; Variable pattern; May mimic migraines or tension headaches
Investigations: Detailed drug history; Review recent changes; Imaging if red flags
Initial/conservative management: Medication review; Avoid overuse of analgesics; Patient counseling
Differential red flags: New neurological symptoms; Severe or worsening pattern

Key features: Sudden onset; Severe (worst ever); Peaks in seconds; May be associated with neurological symptoms

Condition: Chronic Sinusitis

source_title: Evaluation of Headache in Adults: A Clinical Flow Chart Guide

Condition: Uncontrolled Hypertension
Key features: Dull, throbbing headache (often occipital); Associated with dizziness; Blurred vision; Fatigue; BP usually markedly elevated
Investigations: BP measurement; Fundoscopy; Renal function tests; ECG; Urinalysis
Initial/conservative management: Lifestyle modification; Salt restriction; Regular monitoring; Medication adherence
Differential red flags: BP > 180/120 mmHg; Chest pain; Breathlessness; Neurological deficit; Papilledema

source_title: Guideline Based Management of Primary Dysmenorrhea: A Clinical Flow Chart Guide
condition_name: Mild Primary Dysmenorrhea (Minimal impact on daily activities)
text:
Condition: Mild Primary Dysmenorrhea (Minimal impact on daily activities)
Key features: Cramping lower abdominal pain at onset of menses; Mild-moderate intensity; Little or no interference with daily activities; No associated significant symptoms
Initial/conservative management: Non-Pharmacologic Measures: Education & reassurance, Heat therapy, Regular exercise, Adequate sleep, Stress reduction (yoga, relaxation), Dietary measures
Advanced/specific management: Second-Line / Adjunctive (If inadequate relief): NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Mefenamic acid, Naproxen, Diclofenac) starting at onset or 1-2 days before menses; Third-Line Options (If persistent pain): Different NSAID agent or dose optimization, Add antispasmodic (e.g., Drotaverine), Magnesium supplement, Vitamin B1 / E
Follow-up: Review in 3-6 months; Assess pain relief, side effects & adherence; Encourage continuation of non-pharmacologic measures; Return earlier if worsening or new symptoms

source_title: Guideline Based Management of Primary Dysmenorrhea: A Clinical Flow Chart Guide
condition_name: Moderate Primary Dysmenorrhea (Interferes with some activities)
text:
Condition: Moderate Primary Dysmenorrhea (Interferes with some activities)
Key features: Moderate to severe cramps; Interferes with school, work or routine activities; May have nausea, vomiting, headache, diarrhoea, backache; Responds to self-care partially
Initial/conservative management: Non-Pharmacologic Measures (as above); NSAIDs (First-line pharmacologic): Start early at onset or 1-2 days before menses
Advanced/specific management: Second-Line / Adjunctive (If inadequate relief): Switch/optimize NSAID, Add antispasmodic, Consider Tranexamic acid (if heavy bleeding), Magnesium / Vitamin B1 / E; Third-Line Options (If persistent pain): COCPs (cyclic or extended), Progestin-only pills, LNG-IUS, Lifestyle & stress management support
Follow-up: Review in 3-6 months; Assess pain score, function & satisfaction; Monitor side effects; Reinforce adherence & non-pharmacologic measures; Step up if inadequate relief

condition_name: Severe Primary Dysmenorrhea (Marked impact / bed rest)
text:
Condition: Severe Primary Dysmenorrhea (Marked impact / bed rest)
Key features: Severe cramping pain; Marked interference with daily activities / school or work absenteeism; Associated symptoms prominent (nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, fatigue); Minimal relief with self-care
Initial/conservative management: NSAIDs (First-line): Adequate dose, early initiation for 2-3 days; Combine with non-pharmacologic measures; Consider antiemetic if severe nausea / vomiting
Advanced/specific management: Second-Line / Adjunctive (If inadequate relief): Switch to another NSAID or higher dose, Add antispasmodic, Add tranexamic acid, Short course simple analgesic (paracetamol) as adjunct; Third-Line Options (Hormonal Therapy): COCPs (cyclic / extended), LNG-IUS, Progestin-only options (e.g., DMPA, implant), Consider GnRH agonist (rare; refractory cases under specialist care)
Follow-up: Review in 3 months; Assess pain relief, quality of life & side effects; Monitor BP (if on COCP), weight, mood; If inadequate relief, reassess for secondary causes

condition_name: Refractory / Treatment Failure (No adequate relief despite optimal therapy)
text:
Condition: Refractory / Treatment Failure (No adequate relief despite optimal therapy)
Key features: Persistent pain despite optimal medical therapy (3-6 months); Significant impact on quality of life; Consider possibility of secondary dysmenorrhea
Initial/conservative management: Reassess: Confirm diagnosis, Review adherence, Assess severity & pattern, Rule out secondary causes (endometriosis, adenomyosis) if atypical features present
Advanced/specific management: Adjunctive Options: Optimize hormonal therapy, Add adjuncts (neuromodulators e.g. amitriptyline, gabapentin), Pelvic floor physical therapy, Psychological support / CBT; Specialist Referral: Gynecologist / pain specialist, Consider diagnostic laparoscopy (if suspicion of endometriosis), Multidisciplinary approach
Follow-up: Individualized follow-up; Monitor treatment response & adverse effects; Adjust plan as needed; Ensure reproductive counselling if required

source_title: Guideline Based Management of Primary Tremors: A Clinical Flow Chart Guide
text:
Condition: Essential Tremor (ET)
Key features: Bilateral action tremor (postural > kinetic); Usually in hands, may involve head, voice; Gradual onset; Family history common; Improves with small amount of alcohol
Initial/conservative management: Non-pharmacologic: Reassurance, Avoid caffeine & stimulants; Adequate sleep; Stress management; Occupational therapy; Weighted utensils
Advanced/specific management: First-line (Pharmacologic): Propranolol 40-240 mg/day (start low, titrate) OR Primidone 25-250 mg/day (start low, titrate); Combination therapy if inadequate response; Topiramate, Gabapentin, Pregabalin
Follow-up: Review in 4-6 weeks; Assess tremor severity, ADL impact & side effects; Monitor HR & BP (if on beta-blockers); Long-term follow-up

source_title: Guideline Based Management of Primary Tremors: A Clinical Flow Chart Guide
text:
Condition: Parkinsonian Tremor (Resting Tremor)
Key features: Resting tremor (pill-rolling); Asymmetric onset; Decreases with voluntary movement; Associated bradykinesia, rigidity, postural instability
Initial/conservative management: Confirm diagnosis; Evaluate for PD criteria; Review medications; Baseline counseling
Advanced/specific management: Levodopa/carbidopa (start low, titrate); Dopamine agonists; MAO-B inhibitors / COMT inhibitors; Physiotherapy; Advanced/refractory: Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi), Apomorphine / Duodopa
Follow-up: Review in 4-6 weeks; Monitor motor & non-motor symptoms; Watch for medication side effects; Regular neurologist follow-up

source_title: Guideline Based Management of Primary Tremors: A Clinical Flow Chart Guide
text:
Condition: Physiologic Tremor
Key features: Low amplitude, high frequency; Present in all individuals; Enhanced by anxiety, fatigue, medications, caffeine, hyperthyroidism
Initial/conservative management: Identify & remove triggers; Reassurance; Lifestyle modification; Treat underlying cause (e.g., hyperthyroidism)
Advanced/specific management: Usually no specific drug therapy required; If troublesome: Propranolol (10-40 mg PRN) for performance-related situations
Follow-up: Review if persistent or worsening; Monitor after treating underlying cause

source_title: Guideline Based Management of Common and Red Flag Cases of Secondary Dysmenorrhoea: A Clinical Flow Chart Guide
text:
Condition: Endometriosis
Key features: Progressive dysmenorrhoea; Chronic pelvic pain; Deep dyspareunia; Infertility; Dyschezia / dysuria; Tender nodularity (POD)
Investigations: Clinical diagnosis; Pelvic ultrasound; MRI (if deep infiltrating); Laparoscopy (gold standard)
Initial/conservative management: NSAIDs; Combined OCPs or Progestins (continuous); LNG-IUS; Tranexamic acid; Lifestyle & pain measures
Advanced/specific management: GnRH agonists / antagonists; Add-back therapy; Laparoscopic excision / ablation; Multidisciplinary care
Follow-up: Review in 6-12 weeks; Monitor pain & bleeding; Assess fertility goals; Long-term follow-up for recurrence

source_title: Guideline Based Management of Common and Red Flag Cases of Secondary Dysmenorrhoea: A Clinical Flow Chart Guide
text:
Condition: Adenomyosis
Key features: Heavy, painful periods; Chronic dull pelvic pain; Enlarged, tender uterus; Dysmenorrhoea; Menorrhagia
Investigations: Clinical evaluation; TVS (bulky uterus, heterogeneous myometrium); MRI (if needed)
Initial/conservative management: NSAIDs; LNG-IUS; Progestins; Tranexamic acid; Iron for anemia
Advanced/specific management: GnRH agonists; Uterine artery embolization (selected cases); Hysterectomy (definitive, completed family)
Follow-up: Review in 6-12 weeks; Monitor bleeding & pain; Manage anemia; Long-term follow-up

Condition: Uterine Fibroids
Key features: Heavy bleeding; Severe dysmenorrhoea; Pelvic pressure; Infertility / recurrent pregnancy loss; Enlarged uterus
Investigations: Pelvic examination; TVS (first line); MRI (mapping); Hb, TFT if indicated
Initial/conservative management: NSAIDs; Tranexamic acid; LNG-IUS (if cavity not distorted); Combined OCPs; Iron supplementation
Advanced/specific management: GnRH agonists (pre-op); Myomectomy; Uterine artery embolization; Hysterectomy (completed family)
Follow-up: Review in 6-12 weeks; Assess bleeding, pain, fertility; Monitor Hb & iron; Long-term follow-up

Condition: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID)
Key features: Bilateral lower abdominal pain; Dysmenorrhoea; Fever, abnormal discharge; Dyspareunia; Cervical motion tenderness
Investigations: Clinical diagnosis; NAAT for GC/CT; CRP / ESR; TVS (TOA); Pregnancy test
Initial/conservative management: Empiric antibiotics (per guidelines); NSAIDs; Partner treatment; Abstain till completion
Advanced/specific management: Hospitalize if severe / TOA; IV antibiotics; Drainage of abscess (if large); Surgical intervention (rare)
Follow-up: Review in 48-72 hrs; Test of cure (if indicated); Counsel on STI prevention; Screen for complications

Condition: Chronic Endometritis
Key features: Chronic pelvic pain; Dysmenorrhoea; Abnormal uterine bleeding; Infertility / implantation failure
Investigations: Clinical suspicion; Endometrial biopsy (plasma cells); Culture / NAAT; HSG (if infertility)
Initial/conservative management: Antibiotics (e.g., doxycycline); Treat underlying cause; Probiotics (adjunct)
Advanced/specific management: Extended antibiotic course if persistent; Manage associated conditions
Follow-up: Review in 4-6 weeks; Reassess symptoms; Repeat evaluation if needed

Condition: Ovarian Cyst
Key features: Acute or cyclic pelvic pain; Dysmenorrhoea; Bloating / fullness; Adnexal tenderness
Investigations: TVS (first line); Beta-hCG (exclude pregnancy); Doppler (torsion)
Initial/conservative management: NSAIDs; Combined OCPs (prevention); Reassurance (functional cysts)
Advanced/specific management: Laparoscopic cystectomy (persistent/symptomatic); Manage torsion urgently; Malignancy evaluation (if suspicious)
Follow-up: Review in 6-12 weeks; Repeat US if indicated; Counsel on warning signs

source_title: Evidence Based Management of Vaginal Discharge in Females: A Clinical Flow Chart Guide
text:
Condition: Bacterial Vaginosis (BV)
Key features: Thin, homogeneous, grey-white discharge; Fishy odour (especially after intercourse); Minimal itching; pH > 4.5; Clue cells on microscopy; Positive whiff test
Investigations: Amsel criteria (>=3 of 4); Nugent score (7-10); pH > 4.5; Microscopy
Initial/conservative management: Metronidazole 500 mg PO BD x 7 days OR; Metronidazole gel 0.75% 5 g intravaginally OD x 5 days OR; Clindamycin cream 2% 5 g intravaginally HS x 7 days
Advanced/specific management: Recurrent BV: Metronidazole gel 0.75% twice weekly x 4-6 months; Consider oral probiotics; Treat sexual partners (not routinely recommended)
Follow-up: Review in 1-2 weeks; Advise to return if symptoms persist or recur; Avoid douching
red_flags: Foul smelling discharge with fever / pelvic pain
Recurrent or persistent discharge not responding to treatment

text:
Condition: Vulvovaginal Candidiasis (Yeast Infection)
Key features: Thick, white, 'cottage cheese' discharge; Intense itching & redness; Burning micturition / dyspareunia; Normal pH (<= 4.5); No fishy odour
Investigations: KOH wet mount: Budding yeast / pseudohyphae; Culture if recurrent or complicated
Initial/conservative management: Fluconazole 150 mg PO, single dose OR; Clotrimazole 1% cream 5 g intravaginally HS x 7 days OR; Miconazole 2% cream HS x 7 days
Advanced/specific management: Recurrent (>=4/year): Fluconazole 150 mg every 72 h x 3 doses, then weekly x 6 months; Consider prolonged therapy in uncontrolled diabetes; Avoid irritants
Follow-up: Review in 1-2 weeks; Check blood sugar if recurrent; Counsel on hygiene
red_flags: Foul smelling discharge with fever / pelvic pain
Recurrent or persistent discharge not responding to treatment

text:
Condition: Trichomoniasis
Key features: Frothy, yellow-green discharge; Foul odour; Itching, irritation; Strawberry cervix (may be present); pH > 4.5
Investigations: Wet mount: Motile trichomonads; NAAT (most sensitive); pH > 4.5
Initial/conservative management: Metronidazole 2 g PO single dose OR; Metronidazole 500 mg PO BD x 7 days (Preferred in women)
Advanced/specific management: Treat all sexual partners simultaneously; Abstain from sex until treatment completed & symptoms resolved; Consider test of cure in pregnancy
Follow-up: Review in 2-4 weeks; Retest if symptoms persist or recur; Screen for other STIs

Condition: Cervicitis (STI-related)
Key features: Mucopurulent discharge; Intermenstrual spotting / postcoital bleeding; Dysuria, dyspareunia; Cervical motion tenderness; Risk factors for STIs
Investigations: NAAT for Chlamydia trachomatis & Neisseria gonorrhoeae; Gram stain (PMNs); Culture if needed
Initial/conservative management: Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM single dose PLUS; Doxycycline 100 mg PO BD x 7 days (If Chlamydia not excluded)
Advanced/specific management: Add Metronidazole 500 mg BD x 7 days if BV co-infection suspected; Treat all partners; HPV vaccination if eligible
Follow-up: Review in 1-2 weeks; Retest for Chlamydia in 3 months; Counsel on safe sex

Key features: Thin, white or clear discharge; No odour, no itching; Varies with cycle; Normal pH (<= 4.5)
Investigations: Clinical diagnosis; Normal pH; No pathogens on microscopy
Initial/conservative management: Reassurance; No medications needed; Counsel on genital hygiene & cotton underwear

Follow-up: Routine care; Return if symptoms change

Condition: Atrophic Vaginitis
Key features: Thin, watery discharge; Vaginal dryness; Itching, burning, dyspareunia; Postmenopausal
Investigations: Clinical diagnosis; pH > 4.5; Vaginal atrophy on exam
Initial/conservative management: Vaginal moisturizers (regular use); Lubricants for intercourse; Topical estrogen cream (as per guidelines)
Advanced/specific management: Low dose vaginal estrogen (e.g., estradiol cream 0.5 g HS x 2 weeks, then 2-3 times/week); Ospemifene (oral) in selected cases
Follow-up: Review in 4-6 weeks; Monitor symptoms; Consider bone health evaluation

Condition: Non-infectious Causes (Allergic / Irritant)
Key features: Discharge with itching & irritation; History of new soap, pads, lubricants, spermicides, etc.; No systemic symptoms
Investigations: Clinical diagnosis; pH normal or mildly elevated; No pathogens
Initial/conservative management: Remove offending agent; Barrier protection (zinc oxide); Topical corticosteroid (short course if severe)
Advanced/specific management: Patch testing in selected cases; Treat secondary infection if present
Follow-up: Review in 2-4 weeks; Return if no improvement
